elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, etc.)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: URL identifier present but not a persistent identifier like DOI or RRID. Project has grant number OT2OD032701 but no DOI assigned to dataset.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI; description: >300 chars covering project scope, data modalities, target enrollment, and current status
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive title and detailed description explaining dataset purpose, scope (100K+ patients, 14 centers), modalities (EHR, waveforms, imaging, EEG, notes), standards (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB), and current status (45K+ admissions, 1.6B rows).

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [CHoRUS, Bridge2AI, critical care, acute illness, AI-ready dataset, OMOP Common Data Model, electronic health records, EHR, waveform telemetry, medical imaging, DICOM, EEG, clinical notes, OHNLP, health equity, social determinants of health, federated access, multi-modal data, high-resolution data, ethical AI, trustworthy AI, workforce development, data standardization, privacy preservation, bias mitigation, ICU, intensive care]
sub_elements.quality_note: 27 relevant keywords covering domain (critical care, ICU), methods (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP), modalities, ethical considerations, and technical aspects.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Landing Page or Platform URL
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: Active project website with dataset overview, team information, and access instructions.

sub_elements.name: Associated Project or Program
sub_elements.evidence: keywords include 'Bridge2AI'; description mentions 'Bridge2AI data generation project'; external_resources include Bridge2AI program links
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear association with NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program, one of four data generation projects.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Mechanism Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license: Controlled Access - Data Use Agreement Required (OT2OD032701); license_and_use_terms section describes registration with institutional email and signed licensing agreement
sub_elements.quality_note: Controlled access model clearly defined with secure enclave (Azure-based infrastructure), institutional email requirement, and license agreement process.

sub_elements.name: Data Use Agreement Required?
sub_elements.evidence: All participants must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access to the dataset; Data use agreement specifies permitted research uses and prohibits re-identification
sub_elements.quality_note: DUA requirements explicitly stated with specific prohibitions (re-identification) and permitted uses (research purposes). Contact information provided for access requests.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats specify access_urls: https://chorus4ai.org/ for all five data modalities (OMOP, WFDB, DICOM, OHNLP, EDF+/Persyst)
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform access URL provided for all data formats via secure enclave. Registration and approval process described.

sub_elements.name: File Formats Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: OMOP Common Data Model (structured EHR), WFDB (waveforms), DICOM (imaging), OHNLP tokenized (clinical notes), EDF+/Persyst (EEG)
sub_elements.quality_note: Five specific standard formats documented with comprehensive metadata schemas and data volumes (1.6B rows OMOP, 23TB WFDB).

sub_elements.name: External Links to Similar or Related Datasets
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: CHoRUS GitHub (28 repositories), NIH RePORTER, Bridge2AI program, AIM-AHEAD training partnership, OHDSI community
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive external resources including GitHub organization, parent program (Bridge2AI), related communities (OHDSI), and training partnerships (AIM-AHEAD).

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: Controlled access with signed licensing agreement; data use agreement specifies permitted research uses; research purposes allowed
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear license terms permit research reuse under controlled access with DUA. Prohibits re-identification but enables AI/ML research, external validation, health equity studies, and educational uses.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model, WFDB (WaveForm DataBase), DICOM, OHNLP open source schema, EDF+ (European Data Format), Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: All five data modalities use recognized international standards enabling interoperability with OHDSI tools, PhysioNet ecosystem, medical imaging systems, and NLP pipelines.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model transformation with OHDSI tool stack; DICOM schema; WFDB format per extended PhysioNet schema; OHNLP open source schema; EDF+ and Persyst open source schemas
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance to five major community schemas explicitly documented with metadata specifications published. OMOP vocabulary standards and semantic mappings validated via chorus-mapping repository.

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Defined for Linking
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit identifiers_in_files field; sensitive_elements mention patient identifiers exist but are de-identified
sub_elements.quality_note: Patient identifiers mentioned in context of de-identification (PHI removal) but no explicit documentation of linking keys or identifiers available for cross-dataset integration.

sub_elements.name: Documentation of Processing Tools for Reproducibility
sub_elements.evidence: GitHub organization (chorus-ai) with 28 repositories including: chorus_waveform (WFDB conversion scripts), privacy_scan_tool (privacy scanning), CHoRUSReports (characterization), chorus-extract-upload (data extract tools), UF-Geocoding (OMOP Location geocoding via DeGauss)
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive open-source tooling with specific repositories for each processing step. MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses. Standard operating protocols in Chorus_SOP repository.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review Documented
sub_elements.evidence: Retrospective data collection from critically ill patients approved through institutional review processes at 14 data acquisition centers; IRB protocols at each contributing site
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive IRB documentation with institutional review at all 14 data acquisition centers. Community-facing ethics focus groups conducted. Legal and ethical advisory teams from multiple disciplines (law, ethics, health services).

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: Re-identification limitation transformations; OMOP transformation for EHR de-identification; DICOM de-identification pipeline; OHNLP tokenization for clinical notes; privacy-preserving transformations; DeGauss geocoding for Location entities
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple de-identification methods documented per data modality: OMOP transformation with privacy scanning, DICOM header de-identification, OHNLP tokenization approach, privacy_scan_tool for medical records. HIPAA compliance emphasized.

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Removed or Masked
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements describe PHI in EHR data, demographics, patient identifiers being de-identified; DICOM metadata de-identification removes embedded patient information
sub_elements.quality_note: De-identification processes described for multiple data types but no explicit enumerated list of specific identifiers removed (e.g., names, dates, SSNs, MRNs). Sensitive element categories identified but not removal inventory.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit consent field found; retrospective data collection mentioned but consent process not documented
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent procedures not explicitly documented despite comprehensive ethics review documentation. Retrospective collection from 14 sites but no statement on waiver of consent, broad consent, or opt-out mechanisms.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Sourcing Statement Included
sub_elements.evidence: Dataset described as 'ethically sourced' in title and description; human_subject_research section details patient-focused efforts to manage privacy and bias; community-facing ethics focus groups determine appropriate data for public sharing; Social Determinants of Health considered
sub_elements.quality_note: Strong ethical sourcing statements throughout. Three-pillar structure (Data, Ethics, People) guides project. Community engagement via ethics focus groups. Training curriculum includes ethics of AI in clinical practice. Emphasis on health equity and trustworthy AI.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Population Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: instances: Critically ill patients requiring acute or critical care admitted to ICU, PICU, NICU across 14 data acquisition centers spanning 20 academic centers; retrospective data collection; target enrollment exceeds 100,000 patients
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive population description including care settings (ICU/PICU/NICU), institutional diversity (14 hospitals, 20 academic centers), geographic distribution (United States), and enrollment targets with current status.

sub_elements.name: Number of Participants or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: As of August 2025: 14 different hospitals, over 45,000 unique admissions, 50,000 patient admissions released (ICU/PICU/NICU), target exceeds 100,000 critically ill patients
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific participant counts with temporal reference (August 2025), current vs. target enrollment, and breakdown by care setting. Transparency about dataset growth trajectory.

sub_elements.name: Modalities or Data Types Listed
sub_elements.evidence: subsets describe five modalities: structured EHR (OMOP), waveform telemetry (WFDB), medical imaging (DICOM), clinical notes (OHNLP tokenized), EEG waveforms (EDF+/Persyst); description mentions multi-modal data
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive modality listing with six subsets documented including formats, access status, current availability, and data volumes for each modality.

sub_elements.name: Conditions or Phenotypes Represented
sub_elements.evidence: description mentions 'acute illness' and 'critically ill patients'; purposes address 'improving recovery from acute illness'; no explicit enumeration of specific conditions or phenotypes
sub_elements.quality_note: General description of critical care and acute illness populations but no specific condition groups, phenotype enumerations, or disease categories documented. Emphasis on comprehensive patient conditions but not listed.

sub_elements.name: File Dimensions or Sampling Rates Provided
sub_elements.evidence: 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data; 23 TB of waveform data; 7,642 admissions with radiology data; 1,000 images currently available; high-frequency documentation in nursing flowsheets; dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific data dimensions and volumes provided: row counts for structured data, storage sizes for waveforms, image counts, and temporal resolution descriptions (high-frequency, time-stamped dosing).

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No dataset_version or version field found in YAML
sub_elements.quality_note: Dataset lacks version number despite being actively updated and expanded. Status described as 'August 2025' snapshot but no formal versioning scheme.

sub_elements.name: Version History Documented
sub_elements.evidence: No release_notes or version history field found
sub_elements.quality_note: No release notes or change log documenting dataset evolution from initial release through current 45K+ admissions state.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions for Each Version
sub_elements.evidence: No version-specific change descriptions found
sub_elements.quality_note: Updates described as continuous but no discrete version releases with change descriptions documented.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates section: Ongoing data collection and continuous expansion; Dataset updated continuously through November 30, 2026; frequency: Continuous updates through November 30, 2026; regular site status updates via GitHub or Google Form
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear update schedule with end date (November 2026), continuous update model, and status tracking mechanisms (GitHub project management, site status forms). Current status vs. target enrollment transparent.

sub_elements.name: Versioned Documentation or External References
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources include GitHub repositories and published paper but not version-specific documentation links
sub_elements.quality_note: GitHub repositories and publication DOI provided but no version-specific documentation. Publication references single methodology paper, not versioned releases.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Rationale for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes section with four detailed purposes: improve recovery from acute illness, create AI-ready critical care dataset (100K+ patients), establish data standards and tools (OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/OHNLP unification), promote diversity and health equity; addressing_gaps section with four gaps addressed
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive motivation across four purposes and four gaps addressed. Rationale spans scientific (AI for critical care), technical (standards unification), ethical (privacy and bias), and educational (workforce development) dimensions.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objective or Task
sub_elements.evidence: tasks section with five tasks: characterize acute/critical care illness, predict complications, measure treatment response, external validation for AI marketplace, label data for prediction targets; intended_uses specify AI/ML model development as primary use
sub_elements.quality_note: Five specific tasks documented with examples. Primary objective clear: develop AI/ML models for characterizing illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response in critically ill patients.

sub_elements.name: Funding Source or Grant Agency Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, administered by NIH Office of the Director
sub_elements.quality_note: Funding agency clearly identified as NIH Common Fund with specific program (Bridge2AI) and administering office documented.

sub_elements.name: Award Number or Grant ID Present
sub_elements.evidence: National Institutes of Health grant OT2OD032701 (project number 1OT2OD032701-01); Opportunity Number: OTA-21-008; Assistance Listing Number: 93.310
sub_elements.quality_note: Complete grant identification with award number (OT2OD032701), full project number (1OT2OD032701-01), opportunity number, and assistance listing number. Award details include fiscal year (2022), funding amount ($5,880,300 direct costs), and project dates.

sub_elements.name: Acknowledgement of Platform or Participant Support
sub_elements.evidence: creators section with 19 individuals (Contact PI Eric S. Rosenthal at MGH, PIs at UF/UT Health/Tufts, lecturers, program managers); maintainers acknowledge 14 data acquisition centers, coordinating teams, Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive acknowledgements with 19 named creators including roles and institutional affiliations. Maintainers section recognizes multi-institutional consortium structure, contributing hospitals, and specialized teams.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Setting or Sites Described
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms describe retrospective EHR extraction at 14 data acquisition centers; 20 academic centers spanning United States; specific institutions named: Massachusetts General Hospital, University of Florida, UT Health Science Center, Tufts Medicine, Emory
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive collection setting documentation with 14 data acquisition sites across 20 academic centers. Lead institutions identified with specific roles. Multi-center federated access model described.

sub_elements.name: Data Capture Method or Device Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: EHR systems for structured data, bedside monitors via gateway/middleware for waveforms, hospital PACS for imaging, hospital EEG databases for EEG; OMOP transformation, OHNLP tokenization, DICOM from PACS, WFDB from bedside monitors
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific data capture devices and systems documented per modality: EHR systems, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, PACS systems, EEG databases. Acquisition workflows described with technical details (dosing time-stamps, high-frequency documentation).

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing or Cleaning Steps Documented
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: OMOP CDM transformation with validated semantic mappings, OHNLP tokenization pipeline, WFDB standardization via chorus_waveform scripts, DICOM de-identification, re-identification limitation transformations; cleaning_strategies: multi-center harmonization via chorus-mapping repository, schema compliance validation
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive preprocessing and cleaning documentation across five strategies and two cleaning approaches. Each modality has specific transformation pipeline documented with quality assurance steps and validation processes.

sub_elements.name: Open-Source Processing Code Provided
sub_elements.evidence: GitHub organization chorus-ai with 28 repositories including: chorus_waveform (MIT license), privacy_scan_tool (Python), CHoRUSReports (R), chorus-extract-upload (MIT license), UF-Geocoding, chorus-mapping (semantic mappings), Chorus_SOP (Apache-2.0 license documentation)
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive open-source code ecosystem with 28 GitHub repositories covering all processing steps. Specific repositories for waveform conversion, privacy scanning, OMOP characterization, data extraction, geocoding, semantic mapping, and SOPs.

sub_elements.name: External Standards or References Cited
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: peer-reviewed publication at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12028-024-02007 (Neurocritical Care journal); OHDSI community OMOP CDM reference; Standards include OMOP, DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet, OHNLP, EDF+, Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Publication DOI provided for methodology paper in peer-reviewed journal. Six international standards referenced (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP, EDF+, Persyst) with community links (OHDSI) for technical specifications.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Limitations Section Present
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses section includes awareness of ongoing data collection limitations: dataset actively growing, cohort coverage varies by modality, EEG extraction and imaging de-id in process, clinical notes stored locally
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations discussed within discouraged_uses context but no dedicated standalone limitations section. Completeness constraints noted (45K current vs. 100K+ target) and modality-specific progress transparently reported.

sub_elements.name: Sampling Bias or Representativeness Noted
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies: federated access enables balanced and diverse cohort; sampling to ensure comprehensive patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies; community ethics focus groups determine appropriate data sharing; Social Determinants of Health contextual factors included; geographic diversity emphasized
sub_elements.quality_note: Representativeness proactively addressed through federated multi-center sampling for balanced/diverse populations. SDOH variables included. Institutional and geographic diversity documented across 14 hospitals. Community input on data appropriateness.

sub_elements.name: Quality Control or Validation Steps Mentioned
sub_elements.evidence: cleaning_strategies: validated semantic mappings via chorus-mapping repository with clinical validation SOP; schema compliance validation against OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/OHNLP/EDF+/Persyst specifications; cross-site data quality checks through CHoRUSReports characterization reports; quality assurance of OMOP transformation
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive QC documentation including semantic mapping validation by clinical experts, schema compliance verification for all modalities, cross-site quality checks via characterization reports, and standard operating protocols for validation workflows.

sub_elements.name: Known Risks or Use Constraints Listed
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses: clinical decision-making without proper validation/regulatory approval (models for research only, require FDA clearance for clinical use); re-identification attempts prohibited (violate DUA, HIPAA, ethical principles); awareness of dataset completeness limitations during ongoing collection
sub_elements.quality_note: Three explicit discouraged uses documented with rationale: premature clinical deployment without validation/approval, re-identification attempts violating agreements/regulations, and use without awareness of ongoing expansion limitations.

sub_elements.name: Conflicts of Interest Declared
sub_elements.evidence: No conflicts_of_interest field found in ethics section or elsewhere
sub_elements.quality_note: No conflict of interest statement despite comprehensive ethics documentation. Funding transparency provided but COI disclosure absent.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: Distribution via https://chorus4ai.org/ secure enclave (Azure-based infrastructure); controlled access with institutional email and licensing; CHoRUS Consortium maintains multi-institutional platform
sub_elements.quality_note: Published on project-specific institutional platform (CHoRUS secure enclave) with robust access infrastructure. Not on generalist repositories (PhysioNet/Dataverse) but on purpose-built controlled-access platform for multi-modal critical care data.

sub_elements.name: Cross-referenced DOIs or Related Dataset Links
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources include published research DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s12028-024-02007 (Neurocritical Care journal documenting CHoRUS dataset methodology and design)
sub_elements.quality_note: Publication DOI provided linking to peer-reviewed methodology paper. NIH RePORTER project link (grant 10472824) cross-references funding record.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Reference
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model with OHDSI tool stack; DICOM schema; WFDB format per PhysioNet schema (extended); OHNLP open source schema; EDF+ and Persyst open source schemas; validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping repository
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive community standards integration across five data modalities. OMOP/OHDSI ecosystem central to structured data. International standards (DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet, EDF+) with published schemas. Semantic mappings maintained via collaborative repository.

sub_elements.name: Associated Outreach Materials
sub_elements.evidence: GitHub organization with 28 repositories including Chorus_SOP documentation site with interactive workflow diagrams; intended_uses include AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI training program (Cohorts 1 and 2, 2024-2026) with Jupyter Notebooks and OHDSI/OMOP workshops; educational use for next generation of AI scientists
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive outreach: comprehensive SOP documentation site, 28 GitHub repositories with tools/tutorials, two cohorts of AIM-AHEAD training program with hands-on Jupyter Notebooks, workshops on OMOP and clinical AI, community discussions via GitHub.

sub_elements.name: Similar Dataset Links or Thematic Grouping
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Bridge2AI program (https://bridge2ai.org/ and https://bridge2ai.org/chorus) as one of four data generation projects; AIM-AHEAD partnership (https://aim-ahead.net/); OHDSI community (https://www.ohdsi.org/)
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear thematic grouping as Bridge2AI data generation project with links to parent program and sister projects. Partnership with AIM-AHEAD for training. Integration with OHDSI observational health data community.

strengths: Comprehensive access and retrieval documentation with clear controlled-access model, DUA requirements, and platform URLs for all five data modalities
Exceptional scientific motivation and funding transparency with detailed purposes (4), tasks (5), gaps addressed (4), NIH grant details, and comprehensive creator acknowledgements (19 individuals)
Outstanding technical transparency with collection settings at 14 sites documented, specific data capture devices/systems, extensive preprocessing pipelines, and 28 open-source GitHub repositories
Strong data standardization across five modalities using community standards (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP, EDF+) with validated semantic mappings and comprehensive tool ecosystem
Excellent cross-platform integration as Bridge2AI project with OHDSI community ties, publication DOI, extensive outreach (AIM-AHEAD training, GitHub documentation, workshops)
Robust ethical oversight with IRB approval at 14 centers, multiple de-identification methods per modality, community ethics focus groups, and strong ethical sourcing statements
Clear composition and structure with specific participant counts (45K+ current, 100K+ target), five modalities documented, and data volumes specified (1.6B rows, 23TB waveforms)
weaknesses: No persistent identifier (DOI or RRID) assigned to the dataset itself, only URL identifier (https://chorus4ai.org/) and publication DOI
Absent formal versioning system despite active dataset growth from 45K to 100K+ admissions - no version numbers, release notes, or change descriptions
Informed consent procedures not documented despite comprehensive IRB and ethics review coverage across 14 sites
No conflict of interest declaration despite extensive funding and multi-institutional collaboration
Missing explicit enumeration of identifiers removed during de-identification (e.g., names, dates, SSNs) - processes described but not inventory of removed fields
No dedicated limitations section - limitations discussed within discouraged_uses but not consolidated standalone disclosure
Identifiers for cross-dataset linking not explicitly defined - patient IDs mentioned in de-identification context but not as linking keys
Specific disease conditions and phenotypes not enumerated despite comprehensive critical care scope
recommendations: Request DOI assignment from Zenodo, Dataverse, or institutional repository to provide persistent identifier alongside project URL
Implement formal versioning scheme (e.g., v1.0 for 50K admissions, v2.0 for 100K) with release notes documenting enrollment growth, new modalities added, and schema changes
Add collection_process.consent field documenting consent approach for retrospective collection (waiver of consent, broad consent, opt-out mechanism) approved by 14 site IRBs
Include ethics.conflicts_of_interest statement documenting any potential conflicts among 19 creators, funders, or institutional partners
Add deidentification_and_privacy.examples_of_identifiers_removed field enumerating specific PHI elements removed: names, dates (HIPAA 18 identifiers), MRNs, geographic subdivisions smaller than state

Create dedicated limitations section documenting: current enrollment status (45K/100K), modality-specific completeness (EEG extraction ongoing, imaging de-id in process), site-level variations, retrospective data constraints
Define data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files documenting available linking keys (encounter IDs, visit IDs in OMOP) for cross-modality integration within CHoRUS and potential external linkage
Add composition.condition_groups enumerating major critical illness categories represented: sepsis, respiratory failure, cardiac events, neurological emergencies, trauma, etc.
